title: AI assistants can connect
highlights: The MCP server for AI assistants starts again: it crashed on start-up, so connecting with your AI access key always failed

title: Plan, replan, and a calmer day
highlights: Plan or Replan any task: Next free slot (you confirm it), Tomorrow first thing, and your own weekend days
Make any task the goal of the day and put your Top 3 in your order, the same on your phone and computer
The calendar's side rail shows Overdue, Today and Inbox, and a time (even one typed in a capture) puts a task on the calendar
Move tasks into a domain, an area or a project, Ctrl+A works on every list, and the sync line stays quiet
New sounds (Felt by default, or Kalimba and Glass), and a short tour with a searchable Guide
Phone polish: a + capture button, tidier Routines, readable short calendar blocks

title: Capture that types, and fills itself in
highlights: Tap Capture to type: on your phone the keyboard comes up with the sheet, and desktop has a Capture button
Hold to talk, or tap the mic in the sheet; on desktop the mic dictates into the field so you can check it first
Write it the way you'd say it: the AI picks up the date, time, priority, length and notes, no !!! or // needed
Whatever the AI filled in shows in a note with Undo, and anything you typed yourself always wins
A What's new page, and a heads-up in Settings → App when an update is ready

title: Your own time zone, and easier projects
highlights: Your own time zone: Today, reminders and the morning digest follow your clock, wherever you are
AI assistants can read and add to your days over MCP, with a key you make in Settings
Rename a project or area from inside it, and change what a thing is: project, retainer, area or domain
Domains can be made, renamed, recoloured, merged and deleted from anywhere
Search results open the thing itself, and a project’s status updates can be edited
Easier number fields: tap to select, or nudge with − and +

title: A tray icon, and paper that becomes tasks
highlights: A tray icon on Windows, with a little flyout: now, next, your Top 3, quick capture and focus
Notifications with buttons — Done and Tomorrow right from a reminder
Quiet hours, and task names hidden on the lock screen until you choose
Paper capture: photograph your handwritten notes and they come back as tasks, events and notes (Arabic too)
Signing up works straight away while email is being set up
Sign-up and reset emails lead back to the app
The chat answers from your day and knows how the app works — in your language
GitHub in Settings leads straight to your issues

title: Settings that tell the truth, and the share sheet
highlights: Settings tells the truth: real reminder times, the real GitHub state, and Google Calendar marked as coming
Kai’s Flow is in the Android share sheet
Make capture keys on the phone
Labels on task rows, and *label to add one
Streak goals for routines
Retainer projects roll their open tasks into the new month

Our own right-click menu
Delete areas
Search in Focus
The calendar snaps to 15 minutes
A default calendar view
Check for updates
A Windows installer that looks like the app
Plan my day searches all your tasks and lets you pick in place
A calendar task opens in one tap
Reminders move with their task
Routines fold by time of day
The pressing ceremony waits for you
Import from Todoist, TickTick, Notion, Obsidian, Kindle and Goodreads
The new icon: a Source Serif K on warm paper
A touch calendar for phones: swipe days, hold to move, resize handles
Open a task as a sheet over any page
A calmer first run
Plan my day and Shut down, redrawn
Our own date and time pickers
Today on the phone, with the NOW slip
Swipe right for Tomorrow, left for Trash with Undo
Hold to select
The refreshed design system
The native Android app

GitHub issues into your Inbox
